_comment: Idea #24 referrer (`sc ref`) — `references[]` NAMES an existing placed ref so the rest of the spec can point at it by `label`. The third sibling of `removals[]` (erase existing) and `overrides[]` (move existing): none of them creates the thing it points at. THIS FILE DEMOS THE CLEAN 'IN-FILE' PATH (plan backlog 🔑): the player placed a chair in-game with `sc pl` (so the exporter emitted it into placements[] with a stable editorId), then aimed at it with `sc ref` and typed a label. ModForge OWNS that object, so build FORCES IT PERSISTENT (0x400 + the cell's Persistent group) — which is exactly what 'a package/alias can target this ref' requires. The label then works in ANY ref field: here Sofia's sandbox package is anchored on 'sofia's chair' with a 128-unit radius + allowSitting, so she keeps coming back to sit in THAT chair. The OTHER path (`ref` = a vanilla "<master>:0xFORMID") is shown in the last entry: vanilla scenery is usually a TEMPORARY ref (a poor specific-reference target), so build warns and `anchor` lets you author a persistent stand-in — "marker" (an XMarkerHeading at the spot: a PLACE to sandbox/travel to) or "replace" (our own persistent copy of the object + a removal of the vanilla original: the anchor IS the object). Coords = the flat Whiterun-stables tundra (ground Z=-4590, same verified spot as scene-export-blacksmith).

npcs.name: Sofia
npcs.greeting: This chair is mine. Find your own.

packages._comment: Sandbox. `location` is the LABEL from references[] — that is the whole point of the primitive. A tight radius + allowSitting = 'sandbox around that chair', which is how vanilla makes an NPC habitually use one piece of furniture.

placements._comment: The chair the player placed in-game with `sc pl`. A plain placement — it is `references[]` that makes it persistent.

references.label: sofia's chair
references.note: she should always come back to this one

references.label: skulvar's hoe
references._comment: The EXTERNAL path, anchor-free: we just NAME a vanilla ref (Skulvar's hoe at the Whiterun stables). Build resolves it in the master link cache, sees it carries no 0x400 flag, and WARNS — the label still resolves, but a quest alias's specific-reference fill or a package SingleRef target may not hold across save/load. Add "anchor": "marker" or "anchor": "replace" (plus base/position/worldspace) to get a persistent anchor of our own.
